title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 48
text:
70. Opposition counsel in a party-and-party case and the State’s representative in tribunals
where the State is the respondent, are expected to draw to the court or tribunal’s attention a
fair picture of the law and not omit cases which go against their side’s interests. They should
be reminded of this.
Giving judgment (the decision)

71. LIPs sometimes do not understand whether they have won or lost their case, even when
judges believe they have been clear. The outcome needs to be plainly stated.

72. Although in the context of represented parties who are vulnerable, chapter 2 provides
interesting examples of Family Court decisions which make a particular effort to be
accessible.

73. Another possibility in appropriate cases is starting the judgment with a short and clear
accessible summary.
